entities.summary:
Octavien de Saint-Gelais (1468–1502) was a French churchman, poet, and translator. He translated the Aeneid into French, as well as Ovid's Heroides, further popularizing the works of the Roman poet. This scholarly endeavor demonstrates the cultural exchange between France and Italy during the late Renaissance, a period marked by the rise of humanism and the revival of classical learning. De Saint-Gelais's translations played a significant role in shaping the French literary canon, influencing generations of writers, including François Rabelais and Pierre de Ronsard.

As a churchman, de Saint-Gelais was deeply invested in the theological debates of his time, often incorporating biblical themes and motifs into his poetry. His works reflect the spiritual and intellectual currents of the late medieval period, a time of great upheaval and transformation in Europe.

The legacy of de Saint-Gelais can be seen in the development of French literature, as well as the broader cultural landscape of the Renaissance. His translations and poetry continue to be studied and admired today, offering insights into the artistic and intellectual practices of 15th-century France.
